newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BORUSSIA MOENCHENGLADBACH PEN PICTURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BORUSSIA MOENCHENGLADBACH PEN PICTURES.

text.p: Pen pictures of Borussia Moenchengladbach players ahead of Saturday's German first division match against Borussia Dortmund:
Uwe Kamps. Goalkeeper. Age 32. Spent all of his top-class career at Moenchengladbach since joining in 1982. Has played more than 300 league games for the club.
Hubert Fournier. Defender. 29. Frenchman who came to Moenchengladbach at start of the season. Plays in middle of defence.
Patrik Andersson. Defender. 25. Swedish international who came from Blackburn Rovers in 1993. Plays alongside Fournier in centre of back four.
Martin Schneider. Midfielder. 28. Defensive midfielder who plays on the left side. Had spells at Bayern Munich and Nuremberg before joining Moenchengladbach in 1990.
Stephan Passlack. Midfielder. 26. Defensive midfielder who has broken into the national squad this season. Joined from Uerdingen at start of season and has made a big impression.
Ioan Lupescu. Midfielder. 28. Experienced Romanian international who came from Bayer Leverkusen at start of season. Operates in defensive role just in front of back four.
Peter Nielsen. Midfielder. 28. Danish international who has been at Moenchengladbach since 1992. Operates on right side of midfield.

Stefan Effenberg. Midfielder. 28. The club's most high profile player. Most of the team's creative play is orchestrated by the tall, blond midfielder. His international career ended at the 1994 World Cup finals when he was sent home for making an obscene gesture at the crowd during a match. National coach Berti Vogts has refused to pick him since.

Peter Wynhoff. Midfielder. 28. Played all his top-class career at Moenchengladbach after joining in 1989. Scored his first goal this season when he came on as a substitute last weekend against Cologne.
Martin Dahlin. Striker. 28. Swedish international who left at end of last season to go to Roma in Italy but returned after a disappointing time there. One goal so far since his return.
Andrzej Juskoviak. Striker. 26. Polish international formerly with Sporting Lisbon. He joined the German club at start of the season. Moenchengladbach's leading scorer with six goals.
Jorgen Pettersson. Striker. 21. Swedish international who has two goals this season.
